title: PostHog vs Google Analytics 4
description: PostHog vs Google Analytics 4 — compare product analytics with funnels and replay versus free web analytics in the Google ecosystem.
verdict: GA4 is a free, general-purpose web analytics platform deeply integrated with Google. PostHog is a product analytics suite with event tracking, funnels, session replay, and feature flags — better for SaaS and app teams.
quickAnswer: **PostHog vs GA4:** PostHog is for product questions (activation, retention, flags); GA4 is for marketing traffic and Google Ads. **PostHog vs Google Analytics:** same split — Google Analytics (GA4) wins on free web reporting and ads linking; PostHog wins when users have accounts and you ship features weekly.
bottomLine: Don't pit these tools as direct competitors unless you only need pageview tracking. For marketing analytics, GA4 (or a privacy alternative) wins on cost and ecosystem. For product teams shipping features weekly, PostHog is the more capable platform.

faq.question: PostHog vs GA4: which should I use?
faq.answer: Use GA4 for marketing-site traffic, Google Ads attribution, and free reporting at scale. Use PostHog when you need product analytics — identified users, funnels, retention, session replay, and feature flags. Many SaaS teams run GA4 on the marketing site and PostHog in the app.

faq.question: PostHog vs Google Analytics: what’s the real difference?
faq.answer: Google Analytics (GA4) is web and campaign analytics in Google’s ecosystem. PostHog is a product analytics suite. They overlap on pageviews, but PostHog is built for in-app behavior and experimentation, while Google Analytics is built for acquisition and media reporting.

faq.question: Is PostHog a Google Analytics alternative?
faq.answer: Yes for basic website traffic reporting, and often a better alternative when product analytics is the job. It is not a drop-in ads-attribution replacement for teams that depend on Google Ads and Search Console linking inside GA4.

faq.question: Is PostHog free?
faq.answer: PostHog Cloud includes 1 million events per month free. GA4 is free for most websites. Compare ongoing costs with our pricing calculator as your event volume grows.

faq.question: Which is better for a SaaS product?
faq.answer: PostHog is generally the better fit for SaaS. It supports user identification, funnels, retention analysis, feature flags, and A/B testing out of the box.

faq.question: Can PostHog be self-hosted?
faq.answer: Yes. PostHog offers open-source self-hosting for teams that want full data control. GA4 is cloud-only through Google.

editorialNotes.title: Use case fit
editorialNotes.content: For a **marketing website or blog**, GA4 or a privacy tool like Plausible is usually enough. For a **SaaS product with user accounts**, PostHog fits better. For **content sites with ad attribution**, GA4 wins. For **feature flags and A/B tests**, choose PostHog. For **free analytics at high traffic**, GA4 has no direct SaaS cost.

afterVerdict: If you only need heatmaps and session recordings for page-level UX — not full product analytics — look at [Hotjar](https://invite.contentsquare.com/analyticsvs) and our [PostHog vs Hotjar](/compare/posthog-vs-hotjar/) comparison.
